newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish higher in light trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish higher in light trade.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished higher in light afternoon trading, keying off Tuesday's firm tone and technical momentum.

December Treasury bond futures climbed through resistance at Friday's 110-10/32 high, triggered mild buy-stops and reached a six-week high at 110-15/32. Traders said resistance now lurks at 110-16/32 and at 110-28/32, the August 19 high.
One dealer was said to be a buyer of at least 6,000 December T-bond contracts in the first half of the session, but that buying dried up later and trade turned very quiet, traders said.

Traders said the early-week bias was bullish heading into Friday's September U.S. employment report. U.S. non-farm payrolls were forecast up 166,000 in September, compared with a 250,000 gain in the previous report. September employment data will be released at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT on Friday.

Some traders said the perception was building that the risk was for a weaker-than-expected payrolls figure, which could launch T-bonds even higher. They said soft jobs growth would most likely keep Federal Reserve policy makers on hold in November, a scenario they said bonds had not yet fully priced in.

"I think that if this number is weak then traders may start looking at the point that we may not see any rate hikes the rest of the year," said Don Pullen, assistant vice president with Dean Witter Reynolds.
"But I still think it's tough to say until we see this number Friday," Pullen said. "I believe that tomorrow is going to be real cautious heading into this number Friday."
Other traders said the jobs data could have less impact on the market than in recent months.
"No Fed policy change is at stake here," said Mike Boss, futures analyst with Aubrey G. Lanston.
"I just get the sense that there is less attention to this one than to the last ten or so," he said.

The Fed stood pat on monetary policy last week, key data on Tuesday was weaker than expected and an Australian newspaper quoted an Australian official saying Fed chief Alan Greenspan downplayed inflation risks.
Boss said good foreign buying of U.S. Treasuries and rallying bond markets overseas furthered the buoyant tone here.
The Chicago Board of Trade estimated bond futures volume on Wednesday at 300,000 contracts, below the 355,732 contracts traded on Tuesday.

December T-bonds closed up 13/32 at 110-10/32, March Eurodollars settled up five basis points to 94.19, March T-bills gained five basis points to 94.72 and December muni-bonds closed up 16/32 at 115-5/32.
